text:
Anthony Gordon scored twice as Barcelona cruised to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday, maintaining Hansi Flick’s side’s push for a top-eight finish with their fourth victory from five league-phase matches.
Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also scored in the space of five second-half minutes for the Spanish champions, who are fourth in the 36-team league table, while the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah are 32nd.
Barcelona had been ‌frustrated for periods ‌in the first half before Adeyemi, filling in on ‌the right wing for the injured Lamine Yamal, delivered a cross that the goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, could only palm to the edge of the six-yard box and Gordon tapped home from close range.
Six minutes after the ‌restart, Pokatilov parried a Jesus effort straight into Gordon’s path and the England forward made no mistake. Adeyemi then scored himself in the 55th minute before Jesus added a fourth as Barcelona’s superior quality began to tell.
Sabah briefly lifted the crowd at the Baku Olympic Stadium when Joy-Lance Mickels found the net after the hour mark.
With goal difference potentially decisive in the race for direct qualification ‌to the last 16, Barcelona continued to press until the final whistle without adding to their tally.
Flick left Lamine out of the travelling squad due to an ankle injury.
In Czechia, Villarreal earned their second win in five Champions League games thanks to Tajon Buchanan’s second-half winner against Slavia Prague. The Canada forward beat Jakub Markovic at his near post to secure a 1-0 win that keeps the Spanish side in contention for a top-24 finish.
Slavia were made to rue a couple of major refereeing decisions being overturned, with the Villarreal defender Renato Veiga initially sent off for an elbow in the first half before it was downgraded to a yellow after a video review. The hosts had a late penalty overturned, too, after Pape Gueye’s challenge on Michal Sadilek was deemed not to be a foul after another look.
